overview:
New York's 25th District leans ten points Democratic, and incumbent Joseph Morelle is seeking another term with every structural advantage intact. He has raised roughly $2.2 million and holds about $468,000 in cash, while Republican Virginia McIntyre has raised about $55,000 and ended the last reporting period with negative cash on hand. No outside groups have spent against Morelle, and prediction markets price his re-election chances near 98 percent.

No public general-election polling is available for this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the incumbency advantage, and the one-sided money race. Those signals all point in the same direction: a comfortable Democratic hold in this Rochester-area seat. The main sources of uncertainty are the absence of polling and the possibility of a late-breaking development, but nothing in the record suggests the district is genuinely in play.
